Their village, a warm, welcoming place for all, is ablaze with black and green fire. A gaunt male elf with long, dark hair is at the center of the inferno, facing off against an *enormous* firbolg woman. She seems to be winning, until Wynne calls out to her for help. The firbolg woman turns, and in that moment, is struck with Feeblemind. All light leaves her eyes as she drops her weapon. The elf laughs, inferno blazing as the rest of the village goes up in smoke, and disappears.

Sitting at the bar in the broken sub pub, Ozgur thinks back to the day he lost his brother. 
as a teenager, Ozgur and his brother Mako went fishing. And after about an hour, they weren't getting any activity. Mako had the brilliant idea to go back to shore, grab a freshly butchered pig, and *Chum the Water.* And it worked! Small bait fish started to appear and then there were larger fish, Warehou, Tarakihi, Snappers and Kingfish. And Sharks.

 Before long the two brothers found themselves in the middle lf a feeding frenzy. The swarm of sharks that appeared flipped their boat and sent them plunging into a whirling cyclone of teeth and blood, Ozgur never saw the Great White until he was in its mouth, being shaken like a ragdoll. Ozgur lost his brother, but gained a healthy respect for sharks.

Web’s druidic circle has a specific tradition surrounding the death of one of its members. This tradition is divided into two sets of rituals, depending on if the subject of the ritual is dying peacefully or preparing for a potentially fatal battle. Either way, the ritual has three parts, the first done two days before the fight or expected passing. The subject of the ritual performs a series of cuts on their body: One down the back of each arm, one along the length of their nose and up their forehead, and one from each ear to the side of their mouth. They then make a few druidic markings on their torso, shoulders, and legs. On each leg are the markings for ‘honor’ and ‘death’. Above the subject’s heart is the marking for ‘life’ and on their stomach and below their collarbones are the markings for ‘memory’ and ‘future’. On each shoulder is the marking for ‘past’. Those important to the subject then drink the blood that flows out of the wounds. If going into a battle, only those who are not going into the same battle will drink of their blood. A special poultice is them applied to the wounds, allowing them to heal but scar intentionally.
    The next day, the subject of the ritual walks around stripped of as many of their clothes as possible, to show their ritual to be witnessed by those around them.
    On the final day, a poultice is applied to the scars by the subject or another close to them preparing them for their potential passing.
